title: Clarify and harden hierarchy-index element ownership
description:
Council multi-round audit found that CreaturePartHierarchyIndex detaches the Parts collection but still exposes the original mutable CreaturePart objects. A caller can mutate hierarchy.Parts[i].Id/ParentId/etc. and mutate the authoritative CreatureDefinition through the supposedly detached index. GetChildren has the same shallow-element issue.

This is deliberately not auto-fixed by deep-cloning the elements: CreatureDefinition.FindPart and hierarchy consumers currently rely on identity-bearing CreaturePart objects, so deep-copying here could silently change public semantics. The work should define whether the index is a read-only traversal view over live elements or a true immutable snapshot, then make that contract structural. Prefer a narrow read-only part projection or internal snapshot type if needed rather than duplicating hierarchy logic.

Parent owner: TSK-0093 malformed-definition hierarchy mechanics. Do not create a parallel graph-mechanics implementation.

Validation gate: focused hierarchy/FindPart/GetChildren tests covering attempted element mutation, identity expectations, duplicate/cycle handling, and canonicalization parity; Unity execution required before closure.
